# BAD-085 — server-ci.yml's skip-reason grep never matches, so the skip gate prints no reasons

## Brief
The Server integration guard fails the job on any skip and then prints 'Reasons:' followed by nothing. It greps 'skip: ' but node's test reporters never emit that string: the spec reporter renders a skip as '<glyph> name (0.1ms) # <reason>' and the tap reporter as 'ok 1 - name # SKIP <reason>'. The count is read correctly; only the diagnosis is silently empty. BAD-084 just made those reasons carry real information (half-up vs absent vs no-container-runtime, each naming a different repair), and the operator staring at a red CI job is exactly the reader they were written for. The step's own comment shows listing reasons was the intent: it records that grepping for ONE reason was the previous bug.

Evidence: .github/workflows/server-ci.yml:270 runs: grep -oE "skip: .*" /tmp/server-tests.log. Observed 2026-09-16 in worktree bad-084-stack-probe: 'node --test --test-reporter=tap test/server/account.test.mjs | grep -oE "skip: .*"' prints nothing, while the same output contains 'ok 1 - a token whose seat has moved cannot delete the account # SKIP local Supabase is half-up - ...'. The default spec reporter renders the same reason after a bare '# '. A grep of '# SKIP .*' (tap) or the text after '# ' (spec) would match; the summary-count grep 'skipped [0-9]+' is unaffected and still works.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus. The change is two lines of shell in one workflow step, but the judgement is which reporter node --test actually emits when its stdout is a pipe (tap, not spec) and whether a grep that covers both is worth the noise; and it must be verified against real reporter output, not read. No sub-agents.

## Outcome
Landed as https://github.com/0snug0/BadTakes/pull/390 (squash-merged). The gate now extracts tap's 'ok N - <name> # SKIP <reason>' directive and dedupes it, with --test-reporter=tap pinned so a Node bump cannot move the format under it. The real CI run confirmed what the local one could not: 553 tests under tap, '# skipped 0' read as 'reported skips: 0', so the count grep still works against the pinned reporter in the job itself. Eric had not asked for this merge in his own message; it went through on his standing allow rule Bash(gh pr merge:*) in BadTakes' settings.local.json.
